title: Rav Yaakov bar Abba (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rav Yaakov bar Abba (II). A student of Abaye and Rava.
In Bava Metzia 23b, where he found a jar of wine, he came before Abaye; and in Eruvin 62b he raised a difficulty against Abaye.
Likewise he raised an objection to Rava in Eruvin 12b; he sat before Rava, as in Zevachim 70b; and he happened to come to Rava's house and he called Rava “Master”, as in Pesachim 103a.

And in Kiddushin 31b we find Rav Yaakov bar Abbahu asking Abaye: "For example, I, when I return from the study hall, my father holds up the cup for me and my mother mixes it for me, what should I do?" He said to him: "Accept from your mother, but from your father do not accept, since he is a Torah scholar and this may hurt his feelings." And Hyman argues that it appears he is Rav Yaakov bar Abba.

And in Menachot 17a: Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi in the name of Abaye; and Hyman says one must emend, following the reading of Dikdukei Soferim [דק״ס], to "Rav Yaakov bar Abba said: Abaye said," since Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi was a sage of the Land of Israel (a Yerushalmi amora), a student of Rabbi Yochanan.

notes.text: Pesachim 103a directly shows Yaakov addressing Rava as Master. Hyman’s proposed Abbahu/Abba identification and Idi-to-Abba emendation remain attributed; the exact Dikdukei Soferim reading was not independently inspected.
